subject: [PATCH v5 5/8] mm/gup: break out gup_lookup_pte() helper

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch breaks out the gup_lookup_pte() helper from the larger follow_page_pte() function in mm/gup.c. The new helper resolves a present PTE to the page it maps, returning NULL if the PTE cannot be followed or a negative errno if the caller must report failure. This change is intended to simplify the code and improve maintainability without introducing any functional changes.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
reviewer suggested adding a comment to handle the case where there's no PMD entry, especially when the PTE PTL is held

Reviewer Lorenzo raised concerns about unclear comments in gup_lookup_pte(), specifically referencing 'the old code' without explanation and using awkward phrasing. They also questioned the necessity of checking for pte_none() and suggested rewording the comment to clearly explain the purpose of deferring page cache access under hugetlbfs.

reviewer questioned the necessity of a local variable that is set true but not used, suggesting it may be dead code and requesting an explanation

Reviewer Lorenzo noted that the patch forgot to include code for need_no_page_table and suggested adding a conditional check using if (!ret && need_no_page_table) return no_page_table(vma, flags, address);, also expressing confusion about the purpose of the patch and suggesting renaming the variable 'need_no_page_table' to something like 'is_none'.
reviews.raw_body:
OK so this is what happens if there's no PMD entry. Maybe worth a comment?
Especially if you have special handling for the PTE PTL being held below.

---

This feels -- a little -- schloppy ;)

Why are you referencing 'the old code' in a permanent comment for which what
'the old code' means is super unclear?

That's really just not helpful.

'A none PTE returns from gup_lookup_pte() before any write check runs' also
reads weirdly.

I'm also not sure why you're sending a pte_none() PTE to gup_lookup_pte()
anyway + checking for the error again?

	if (pte_none(ptep)) {
		... whatever ...
		goto blah;
	}

It seems silly otherwise.


Also isn't the page cache thing _only_ for hugetlbfs, unless you changed
that? And aren't a number of other callers of no_page_table() also broken?

But in general the comment could be made much clearer:

	/*
	 * If a hugetlb VMA it might access the page cache in no_page_table(),
	 * which cannot be done under the PTL, so defer until it's dropped.
	 */

Or whatever, something human-written like that :)

---

This is set true but not used anywhere? This is dead code no? Am I missing
something?

Patches should be incremental but adding completely useless locals incrementally
seems silly?

---

I'm guessing you forgot to include the code that works with
need_no_page_table here?

Should it have been:

	if (!ret && need_no_page_table)
		return no_page_table(vma, flags, address);

Perhaps?

I'm not sure any of this is really a cleanup, I'm finding this quite
confusing, actually...

'need_no_page_table' isn't a great name either. Maybe is_none or something?

can't be introducing completely dead code like that, even incrementally.
